text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: P1 continuous-batcher growth & runtime OOMs in prod-west. Start time 2026-03-10T02:13:20Z. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-082 Please respond.

maria-g: on it. grabbing logs and calling infra.

maria-g: quick summary: GPUs in pool 'batcher-west-1' are showing repeated `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` followed by container OOMKilled. queue depth keeps growing, backpressure not kicking in.

jon-k: I see a big spike in queued->processing ratio in metrics. could be enqueue deadlock or unbounded growth in prefix caching.

kevin-l: pasting pod status for context:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=continuous-batcher -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
batcher-0                               1/1     Running            12         8d
batcher-1                               0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   47         3h
batcher-2                               1/1     Running            3          6d
```

maria-g: logs excerpt: 
```text
2026-03-10T02:12:59Z ERROR runtime::gpu: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at kernel.cu:243
2026-03-10T02:13:00Z WARN batcher::queue: queue length 12456 > config.max_batch_items 1024
2026-03-10T02:13:05Z ERROR containerd: oom killed process pid=4321 cmd=/app/serve
```

ashley-c: I'm seeing customer-facing latency >30s and some 504s from prod-west. CS reports outages for two mid-market customers: FolioHealth and Shoply.

customer-success-bot: Notified FolioHealth support team. Ticket created TKT-7891.

maria-g: mitigation plan (initial):
1) scale down continuous-batcher replicas to 1 to stop growth
2) disable continuous-batcher autoscaling
3) flip config to bounded/batched mode (limits per-batch)
4) drain problematic GPU nodes for nvcrash/dmesg collection

jon-k: how do we flip to bounded? is there a runtime flag?

maria-g: yes. patch config: `kubectl -n runtime patch cm batcher-config --patch '{\"data\":{\"mode\":\"bounded\"}}'` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/continuous-batcher -n runtime`

kevin-l: doing step 1 now: `kubectl scale deployment continuous-batcher --replicas=1 -n runtime` (starting)

incident-bot: Action logged: scaled to 1 replica by kevin-l @ 2026-03-10T02:14:30Z

kevin-l: scaled to 1. still seeing OOMs from CrashLoopBackOffs on restart attempts.

ashley-c: CS update: FolioHealth degraded (heavy latency), Shoply intermittent 504s. Sending status page link.

maria-g: draining node gpu-16 to collect nvcrash logs: `kubectl drain gpu-16 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n runtime`

jon-k: attaching a small gdb backtrace from one core dump we pulled:
```text
#0  0x00007f... cuLaunchKernel
#1  0x000056... runtime::kernel_launch
#2  0x000056... batcher::process_batch
```

maria-g: to reduce memory pressure quickly set env to limit batch size: `kubectl set env deployment/continuous-batcher BATCH_MAX_ITEMS=256 -n runtime`

kevin-l: env set, restarting pods.

maria-g: after reducing BATCH_MAX_ITEMS we see queue drain improve, but one pod still OOMKilled during startup. suspect memory blowup on certain prefixes.

jon-k: if OOMs persist we should route traffic to hosted-fallback (lower perf) until we have dumps. Example curl to swap routing: 
```
curl -XPOST https://internal-api/routes/swap -d '{ "route":"continuous-batcher","fallback":"hosted-fallback" }' -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
```

ashley-c: CS asks: estimated customer impact window?

maria-g: approx 12-20 minutes so far (mitigation started ~02:13 -> now ~02:35). We'll confirm after next check once queue drains.

maria-g: handing off to jon-k for followups. I'll stay until 03:00 if anything pops. Jon: please check nvcrash/dmesg and confirm no kernel-level issues.

jon-k: ack, taking over. Checklist for handoff:
1) collect nvcrash + dmesg from drained nodes
2) run `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` on nodes to inspect memory usage/FB
3) run heap profile on batcher process if we can reproduce in a controlled way
4) coordinate with infra if hardware fault.

incident-bot: Handoff: oncall-change maria-g -> jon-k @ 2026-03-10T02:22:00Z

customer-success-bot: FolioHealth ticket updated: 'Mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m.'

jon-k: initial nvcrash indicates memory corruption patterns on GPU 0, driver 525.85.05 (weird pointers). Opening infra ticket INFRA-456 to escalate driver/hardware possibility.

kevin-l: noted followups to address in postmortem: - run heap/profile in staging on long-prefix workload - add circuit breaker on enqueue path to prevent unbounded growth - add alert at 2k queued items and auto-fallback toggles - add limits on prefix cache size

ashley-c: drafted customer comms PR: https://redwood.internal/wiki/status/INC-2026-082 - please review and sign off.

jon-k: confirmed no kernel panic and no host-level OOMs. leaving notes in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/continuous-batcher. handing to next SRE shift `sre-shift` at 03:00.

sre-shift: taking over at 03:00. please assign me tasks for followup and postmortem.

maria-g: final on-call note before stepping back: suspected cause = continuous-batcher memory growth + pathological queued prefixes triggering kernel illegal-address in some GPU kernels. Mitigations applied: scaled replicas->1, switched bounded mode, set BATCH_MAX_ITEMS=256, drained nodes, created INFRA-456, created CS tickets. Collecting dumps for postmortem.

jon-k: monitoring metrics: queue length 120 -> 80 in the last 5m, error rate down. keeping thread open until stable.

kevin-l: thanks everyone. add me to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-082 logged as 'mitigation in progress' by oncall.
